user.title: Device Setup
user.description: Configure your Tasmota IR air conditioner connection.

data_description.vendor: The IR protocol vendor (e.g., SAMSUNG_AC, ELECTRA_AC, FUJITSU_AC, MITSUBISHI_AC).
data_description.command_topic: MQTT topic for sending IR commands. Usually cmnd/'{device}'/irhvac.
data_description.state_topic: Primary MQTT topic for receiving AC state updates. Use tele/'{device}'/RESULT to capture all IR signals (including physical remote).
data_description.state_topic_2: Optional secondary MQTT state topic. Use stat/'{device}'/RESULT to also capture IR transmission confirmations. Subscribes to both topics if set.
data_description.availability_topic: MQTT topic for device online/offline status. Leave blank to auto-derive from command topic (tele/'{device}'/LWT).
data_description.mqtt_delay: Delay in seconds between MQTT commands. Use when operating multiple devices to stagger high-current peaks.

climate.title: Climate Settings
climate.description: Configure temperature ranges, modes, and fan settings. All fields have sensible defaults.

data_description.ir_protocol_unit: Temperature unit for IR commands sent to the AC. Most AC units use Celsius internally even if your HA or remote displays Fahrenheit. Only change to Fahrenheit if your specific AC model requires it.
data_description.ignore_off_temp: When the AC is turned off via remote, some devices report the lowest temperature. Enable to keep showing the last target temperature instead.
data_description.keep_mode_when_off: Keep the last HVAC mode when turning off. Required for MITSUBISHI_AC, ECOCLIM, and similar devices.
data_description.away_temp: Temperature to use when Away preset is active. Leave blank to disable the Away preset.
data_description.supported_fan_speeds: Note: auto_max/max_high are for devices where the remote shows max but Tasmota reports high, and auto which is actually max.
data_description.supported_preset_modes: Vendor-specific preset modes. Select the presets your unit supports. Leave empty if your unit has no special presets. Custom values can be typed in.

advanced.title: Advanced Settings & Sensors
advanced.description: Configure default modes, swing positions, toggle properties, and external sensors.

data_description.pi_enabled: Enable the PI+feedforward controller for automatic temperature regulation. When enabled, the next step will let you configure PI parameters.
data_description.has_set_vertical_vane: Enable if your unit has a button to cycle the vertical vane to a fixed position. Creates a button entity.
data_description.has_set_horizontal_vane: Enable if your unit has a button to cycle the horizontal vane to a fixed position. Creates a button entity.
data_description.default_quiet_mode: Quiet mode via IRHVAC JSON command. Some vendors ignore this — use vendor-specific presets instead if available.
data_description.default_turbo_mode: Turbo mode via IRHVAC JSON command. Some vendors ignore this — use vendor-specific presets instead if available.
data_description.default_econo_mode: Economy mode via IRHVAC JSON command. Some vendors ignore this — use vendor-specific presets instead if available.
data_description.hvac_model: AC model identifier. Use -1 for auto-detection.
data_description.toggle_list: Properties that don't retain the On state. Set this if your AC has toggle-only controls (pressing the button toggles between on and off rather than setting a specific state).
data_description.special_mode: Mode to enter for special functions like automatic cleaning after operation. Leave blank to disable.
data_description.temperature_sensor: External temperature sensor entity for more accurate room temperature readings.
data_description.power_sensor: Binary sensor or sensor that indicates whether the AC unit is powered on.

pi_gains.title: PID Gains & Deadband
pi_gains.description: Configure the core PID controller parameters.

data_description.pi_kp: Proportional gain. Higher values react faster to temperature errors but may overshoot.
data_description.pi_ki: Integral gain. Eliminates steady-state error over time.
data_description.pi_kd: Derivative gain. Dampens overshoot by reacting to rate of temperature change. Set 0 to disable.
data_description.pi_kd_filter_n: Derivative filter coefficient (2-20). Higher = less noise filtering. Default 8.
data_description.pi_deadband: Temperature range (°C) around setpoint where no adjustments are made. Always in °C regardless of system unit.

pi_seeds.title: Feed-Forward Seeds
pi_seeds.description: Configure the outdoor temperature sensor and initial feed-forward seed coefficients.

data_description.outdoor_temp_sensor: Required for feed-forward and learning subsystems. Without this, only basic PI control is available.
data_description.pi_outdoor_seed_heat: Initial outdoor compensation per degree of outdoor-indoor difference (heating). Positive = outdoor warmth reduces heating needed. The system learns the true value over time.
data_description.pi_outdoor_seed_cool: Initial outdoor compensation per degree of outdoor-indoor difference (cooling). Positive = outdoor warmth reduces cooling needed. The system learns the true value over time.
data_description.pi_intercept_seed_heat: Baseline FF intercept for heating. HP setpoint offset when all features are zero. Usually learned automatically; 0 is a safe starting point.
data_description.pi_intercept_seed_cool: Baseline FF intercept for cooling. HP setpoint offset when all features are zero. Usually learned automatically; 0 is a safe starting point.
data_description.pi_outdoor_seed_clamp_min: Minimum outdoor seed the system can learn. Default 0.0. Widen only if the system recommends it.
data_description.pi_outdoor_seed_clamp_max: Maximum outdoor seed the system can learn. Default 2.0. Most systems stay well within this range.

pi_timing.title: Timing & Filtering
pi_timing.description: Configure timing intervals, IMC tuning, and signal filtering.

data_description.pi_tick_fallback: Maximum seconds between PI ticks. Sensor updates trigger ticks sooner (60s cooldown). This is the fallback if no sensor update arrives.
data_description.pi_response_lag: Heat pump response lag (minutes). Time for a setpoint change to begin affecting room temperature. Used by IMC gain formula and Smith predictor. Default 15 min.
data_description.pi_imc_lambda: IMC closed-loop speed parameter (minutes). Controls aggressiveness of IMC-derived gains. Lower = faster but less robust. 0 = auto (response_lag / 3).
data_description.pi_sensor_filter_tau: Low-pass filter time constant on room temperature sensor (seconds). Smooths noise without adding significant lag. 0 = disabled. Default 120s (2 min).
data_description.pi_setpoint_hold: Minimum seconds between HP setpoint changes. Prevents oscillation from incomplete information. 0 = no hold (not recommended). Default 1200s (20 min).

pi_advanced.title: Advanced PI
pi_advanced.description: Configure setpoint weighting and experimental features. Subsystem toggles (FF, batch WLS, plant ID) are now runtime services — use set_subsystem.

data_description.pi_setpoint_weight: 2-DOF PI setpoint weighting. At 1.0 (default), P reacts fully to setpoint changes. At 0.0, P only reacts to disturbances. Try 0.5 for less overshoot on setpoint changes.
data_description.pi_smith_enabled: Enable Smith predictor for dead-time compensation. Requires IMC (τ estimate > 0). Adjusts proportional term to anticipate HP pipeline delay.
data_description.pi_auto_perturb_enabled: Automatically perturb the setpoint ±1°C when steady state is detected to accelerate plant identification. Temperature may vary ~1°C during learning cycles. Requires IMC (τ estimate > 0).
data_description.pi_auto_perturb_window_start: Optional: only start perturbation cycles during this time window (hour 0-23). Leave empty for anytime.
data_description.pi_auto_perturb_window_end: Optional: end hour of perturbation window (0-23). Leave empty for anytime.
data_description.pi_auto_perturb_research_mode: Research mode: bypass the convergence gate (perturb whenever steady state is detected) and raise the stall cap from 5 to 30 cycles. Cycles where the room moved less than 0.4°C are flagged low-quality and don't count toward stalling. Use this to accumulate enough excitation cycles for offline plant identification (~10-30 cycles per 30-day window expected). Best on a single zone with flexible comfort (e.g., living room overnight via the window settings); avoid on bedrooms during sleep hours.

model_inputs_add.title: Add Model Input
model_inputs_add.description: Add a factor that influences the feedforward model. Best for active heat sources/sinks (pellet stove, oil zone, AC, neighbor heat pump) and adjacent rooms with their own heating. Skip purely passive rooms (a closed-off hallway or unheated guest room) — outdoor temperature and the building's tau already absorb their effect, and the gate will keep them frozen anyway.

data_description.model_input_entity: Entity providing the input value. Binary entities: 1 when on, 0 when off. Numeric entities use their value directly.
data_description.model_input_seed_heat: How much does this warm your room in heating mode? (°C of HP setpoint equivalent). Positive = warms room (solar, stove). The system learns the true value over time.
data_description.model_input_seed_cool: How much does this warm your room in cooling mode? Usually same as heating. Positive = warms room.
data_description.model_input_clamp_min: Minimum allowed coefficient value. Prevents nonsensical learning. Leave empty for no minimum.
data_description.model_input_clamp_max: Maximum allowed coefficient value. Leave empty for no maximum.
data_description.model_input_lag_tau: Exponential lag filter time constant in minutes. Use for thermal sources with ramp-up/down (e.g., pellet stove: 30 min). 0 = no filter.
data_description.model_input_suppress_learning: Pause coefficient learning while this input is active. Use for events you want the controller to react to but not LEARN from — e.g., a window-open contact sensor, a cooking-detect, a vacation-mode toggle. Don't enable for normal heat sources you want the model to predict, since suppressing during firing prevents the system from learning the source's effect.
data_description.model_input_delta_from_room: Compute input as (entity temperature − room temperature). Use for inter-zone heat transfer where the temperature difference between rooms drives heat flow.
data_description.model_input_gate_entity: Binary sensor or switch that gates this input. When the gate is off (or on if inverted), the input value is forced to zero. Use for mode-switching phenomena like door-gated convective heat transfer.
data_description.model_input_gate_invert: Invert the gate logic: force input to zero when the gate entity is on instead of off.
data_description.model_input_input_role: How this input enters the building energy balance. Solar Proxy: radiative gain (window solar). Heat Source: direct heat input (pellet stove, space heater, oil zone, neighbor HP). Adjacent Zone: heat transfer from a neighboring room (party-wall coupling — pair with 'Delta From Room Temperature' so the controller sees the temperature difference, not the absolute reading). Other: generic disturbance.
data_description.model_input_input_enabled: When disabled, the input value is forced to zero but the configuration (seeds, clamps, lag) is preserved.

model_inputs_edit.title: Edit Model Input
model_inputs_edit.description: Select a model input to edit.

model_inputs_edit_form.title: Edit Model Input
model_inputs_edit_form.description: Update the settings for this model input. Active heat sources (stove, oil zone) and adjacent rooms with their own heating learn meaningful coefficients. Purely passive rooms stay frozen — their effect is already absorbed by outdoor and tau.

ir_actions_add.description: Define a new IR action. Buttons send an IR code when pressed. Presets show in the preset dropdown with state tracking.

data_description.ir_action_type: Button: one-shot action, no state. Preset: shows in preset dropdown with state tracking.

data_description.ir_action_auto_clear: Automatically deactivate this preset after N seconds (e.g., 1200 for 20 min). 0 = stay active until manually changed.
data_description.ir_action_pause_pi: Pause the PI controller while this preset is active. Use for modes that override normal temperature control.

outdoor_sensor_not_found.title: Outdoor temperature sensor not found
outdoor_sensor_not_found.description: The PI controller is configured to use outdoor temperature sensor `{entity_id}`, but this entity does not exist in Home Assistant. Feedforward compensation will not work until this is resolved.

model_input_entity_not_found.title: Model input entity not found
model_input_entity_not_found.description: The model input '{name}' references entity `{entity_id}`, but this entity does not exist. Suppress/bias from this input will not work until the entity is available.

temp_sensor_not_found.title: Temperature sensor not found
temp_sensor_not_found.description: The climate entity is configured with temperature sensor `{entity_id}`, but this entity does not exist. PI control and accurate temperature display require this sensor.

slope_divergence.title: {zone_label}: Feedforward slope has drifted ({mode})
slope_divergence.description: Learned {mode} slope: {learned}, configured: {configured} ({drift_pct}% difference). Update your configured slope in Settings → Devices → Configure → PI Controller → {mode_cap} Slope, or press the Save Learned Seeds button to checkpoint all current values.

confirm.title: Update {mode} feedforward slope
confirm.description:
Update configured {mode} slope from {configured} to {learned}.

This aligns the feedforward baseline with what the model has learned from your system's behavior.

save_seeds.title: {zone_label}: Model has converged — review and save learned coefficients
save_seeds.description:
The feedforward model has stabilized. Saving updates the anchor values that the system pulls coefficients toward. Review the learned values below and confirm they make physical sense before saving. Coefficients marked 'uncertain' have high variance and may not be well-determined — saving them anchors the system to a noisy estimate.

{coefficient_summary}

confirm.title: Save learned coefficients

high_integral_immature.title: {zone_label}: High integral correction (model still learning)
high_integral_immature.description: The PI integral is compensating with {correction}°C of setpoint adjustment. No action needed — the model is still learning ({count} of ~100 observations). Performance will improve as the model accumulates more data.

high_integral_slope_gap.title: {zone_label}: High integral correction (slope mismatch)
high_integral_slope_gap.description: Configured {mode} slope: {configured}, learned: {learned}. The integral ({correction}°C correction) is covering this gap. Update your {mode} slope to {learned} in PI Settings to reduce integral load.

high_integral_equipment.title: {zone_label}: High integral correction (equipment at limits)
high_integral_equipment.description: Your heat pump frequently reaches maximum output but cannot maintain the target temperature. This may indicate undersized equipment or a need for professional HVAC service. You can also configure a supplemental heat source in the integration settings.

high_integral_tuning.title: {zone_label}: High integral correction (tuning needed)
high_integral_tuning.description: Integral correction averages {correction}°C. Consider reducing Ki from {current_ki} to {suggested_ki} in PI Settings.

confirm.title: Adjust integral gain (Ki)
confirm.description:
Reduce Ki from {current_ki} to {suggested_ki}.

The current Ki is causing excessive integral correction. Reducing it will make the controller less aggressive but more stable.

model_drift.title: {zone_label}: Persistent model drift on {coeff_name}
model_drift.description: The batch model has corrected {coeff_name} {direction} for {count} consecutive cycles, suggesting a physical change. {suggestion} You can call the reset_ff_seeds service to re-learn, or flush the observation buffer to start fresh.

intercept_absorbing.title: {zone_label}: Intercept absorbing {absorbed_name} effect
intercept_absorbing.description: The intercept has grown to {intercept_value}°C, absorbing the effect of {absorbed_name} (stuck at {absorbed_clamp}). Call the reset_ff_seeds service to re-learn both coefficients. If {absorbed_name} returns to its clamp, consider widening its range in PI Settings.

residual_pattern.title: {zone_label}: Unmodeled disturbance detected ({time_range})
residual_pattern.description: Residuals are consistently {direction} ({mean_residual}°C) between {time_range} across {n_observations} observations. This suggests {cause_hint}. Consider adding a model input for this source.

multicollinearity.title: {zone_label}: Highly correlated model inputs
multicollinearity.description: The information matrix condition number is {condition_number}, indicating multicollinearity. Correlated features: {pairs}. This may cause coefficient estimates to shift between batch cycles. This often resolves on its own as the system sees more varied conditions (e.g. different weather, time of day). No action needed unless coefficients are visibly unstable.

freeze_impact.title: {zone_label}: Frozen coefficient {coeff_name} is degrading model fit
freeze_impact.description: Since freezing {coeff_name} ({mode} mode), batch residual RMS has increased from {rms_at_freeze} to {current_rms} (+{increase_pct}%). The model may need this coefficient to track a real change. Consider unfreezing it, or updating its value with the set_coefficient service and saving seeds.

frequent_exclusions.title: {zone_label}: Consider adding a model input or using suppress_learning
frequent_exclusions.description:
You have excluded observations {count} times. If a recurring event causes these anomalies, consider:

1. Adding a model input with a gate entity (e.g., a door/window binary sensor) to teach the model this pattern
2. Using the suppress_learning entity before the event occurs
3. Setting up a timer-based automation: suppress learning for N hours when the event starts

anomalous_observation.title: {zone_label}: Unusual temperature deviation ({time_range})
anomalous_observation.description:
Detected {direction} (mean residual: {mean_residual}°C, severity: {peak_cusum}). This could indicate an unmodeled heat source or sink such as open windows, cooking, or a space heater.

Excluding these observations prevents them from biasing the model. Dismissing keeps them in the learning buffer.

confirm.title: Handle anomalous observations
confirm.description:
Detected {direction} at {time_range} (mean residual: {mean_residual}°C).

Choose an action:

auto_perturb_stall.title: {zone_label}: Plant identification stalled ({mode})
auto_perturb_stall.description: Auto-perturbation completed {cycles} cycles without meaningful improvement in plant identification confidence. This may indicate insufficient excitation, an unmodeled disturbance, or sensor placement issues. Consider running a full plant test (identify_plant service) or reviewing model inputs.

confirm.title: Reset auto-perturbation
confirm.description: Clear the stall counter and allow auto-perturbation to try again.

outdoor_temp_unavailable.title: {zone_label}: Outdoor temperature sensor unavailable
outdoor_temp_unavailable.description: Sensor `{sensor}` has been unavailable for an extended period. Feedforward learning, observation recording, and plant identification are paused. The controller is running on PI feedback only with a frozen FF offset. Check the sensor connection and entity status.

abort.already_configured: A model input for this entity and gate combination already exists.

user.title: Add Model Input
user.description: Add a sensor or entity that affects room temperature (e.g., solar proxy, pellet stove, door sensor).

data_description.name: Display name for this input.
data_description.entity_id: The sensor or entity to read values from.
data_description.seed_heat: How much does this warm your room? (°C of HP setpoint equivalent). Positive = warms room. The system learns the true value over time.
data_description.seed_cool: How much does this warm your room in cooling mode? Usually same as heating. Positive = warms room.
data_description.lag_tau: Exponential smoothing time constant in seconds. 0 = no filtering.
data_description.suppress_learning: Prevent RLS from updating this coefficient (use seed only).
data_description.delta_from_room: Compute input as (entity temperature − room temperature). Use for inter-zone heat transfer where the temperature difference between rooms drives heat flow.
data_description.typical_value: Expected value when this input is active. Balances learning rates across inputs with different scales. Examples: 1.0 for binary (on/off), 0.5 for solar proxy (0–0.8 range), 1.0 for outdoor temp rate in °C/hr, 2.0 in °F/hr.
data_description.gate_entity: Binary sensor or switch that gates this input. When the gate is off (or on if inverted), the input value is forced to zero. Use for mode-switching phenomena like door-gated convective heat transfer.
data_description.gate_invert: Invert the gate logic: force input to zero when the gate entity is on instead of off.
data_description.input_role: How this input enters the building energy balance. Solar Proxy: radiative gain on building envelope. Heat Source: direct heat input (pellet stove, space heater). Adjacent Zone: heat transfer from neighboring room. Other: generic disturbance.
data_description.input_enabled: When disabled, the input value is forced to zero but the configuration (seeds, clamps, lag) is preserved. Use to temporarily remove an input without losing its settings.

abort.already_configured: A supplemental source for this entity already exists.

user.title: Add Supplemental Heat Source
user.description: Add a heat source with its own thermostat (e.g., pellet stove, oil boiler zone). The HP will defer to this source when it is active.

data_description.name: Display name (e.g., 'Pellet Stove', 'Oil Boiler Zone 1').
data_description.entity_id: The climate entity of the supplemental heat source.
data_description.seed_heat: How much does this source warm your room? (°C of HP setpoint equivalent, e.g., 3.0). Positive = warms room.
data_description.seed_cool: How much does this source warm your room in cooling mode? Usually same as heating. Positive = warms room.
data_description.failure_threshold: Seconds the room must stay below HP desired before the HP assists. Default 900 (15 minutes).
data_description.recovery_margin: Degrees above desired before HP defers again after assisting. Prevents oscillation.
data_description.auto_model_input: Use this source as an input to the feedforward model. The HP will account for this source's thermal contribution when predicting the needed setpoint.
data_description.input_enabled: When disabled, this supplemental source is ignored and its auto-model-input (if any) is not created. Configuration is preserved for re-enabling.
